title: Unphosphorylated tyrosines mediate PD-1 inhibition of T cell signaling condensate formation.

verified.what_i_actually_checked: Europe PMC core record (isOpenAccess=N, inEPMC=N, hasSuppl=N, hasData=N, no text-mined accessions); the only NCBI PMC link (PMC13644036) is the accompanying Perspective commentary by Chakraborty, not the research article, and I read its full text; Zenodo query on the article identifier returned 0 records; Dryad query returned 0 records; PDBe citation-DOI query returned 0 structures; Europe PMC preprint search for a bioRxiv version returned 0 hits; a HEAD request to the Science supplementary-materials URL returned HTTP 403 (subscription wall).
verified.what_came_from_paper_text_only: Everything about the experiments themselves comes from the abstract plus the open-access Perspective commentary: in vitro reconstitution of LAT (linker for activation of T cells) condensates, the PD-1 (programmed cell death protein 1) cytoplasmic domain inhibiting condensation, tyrosine-to-tryptophan substitutions restoring inhibition in T cells. I never saw a methods section, a supplementary table, a figure source-data file, or any row count.

a1_downloadable.note: FAIL, verified. No data exists to download: no accession in Europe PMC, no GEO/SRA/BioProject link, no Protein Data Bank entry citing the DOI, nothing on Zenodo or Dryad, no preprint. The only candidate files are the Science supplementary materials, and that URL returns HTTP 403 (institutional subscription required), which the checklist counts as a login wall.

a2_label_is_a_column.note: Not formally reachable after A1, but worth recording: the measurements in this paper are microscopy images of droplets, biolayer/surface-binding traces and flow-cytometry readouts. Any prediction target (condensate formed yes/no, droplet intensity, saturation concentration) would have to be constructed from figure panels, not read from a column.

a3_inputs_present.note: The only genuine strength: the inputs are short peptide and cytoplasmic-domain sequences (PD-1 ITIM/ITSM motifs, LAT) that anyone can write down from UniProt, so no identifier resolution would be needed. Taken from the abstract, not from a file.

a4_units_stated.note: Unknown and unverifiable. Without the methods or supplement I could not confirm units for any quantity (concentration, partition coefficient, binding affinity).

a5_enough_rows.note: FAIL on the paper's own design. This is a mechanistic reconstitution study: the experimental unit is a protein construct or point mutant, and such papers typically test tens, not thousands. The checklist floor is ~1,500 labelled rows (~400 for classification). I verified no count because no file exists.

a6_fits_laptop.working_set: <0.1 GB if the supplement were ever released; microscopy raw images would be larger but are not deposited.
a6_fits_laptop.note: Size is not the problem here.

a7_counts_match_paper.note: Cannot be checked: there is no download to compare against the paper, and no API record of any dataset.

a8_label_provenance.note: The underlying measurements are direct physical observations (in vitro condensate formation, cellular signalling assays), not another model's output, so provenance would be clean if the data existed.

existing_models.score_and_split: Not retrieved; I saw only the title and an abstract snippet from a web search, so I record no number.

existing_models.score_and_split: Not retrieved; title and abstract snippet only.

existing_models.score_and_split: Not retrieved; title and abstract snippet only.

backbone.name: ESM-2, a protein language model that turns an amino-acid sequence into a numeric vector; small checkpoints run on a laptop CPU
backbone.hardware: CPU only; the sequences here are short (tens to ~100 residues)

integration.partner_dataset: None usable. In principle PhaSePro / DrLLPS / CD-CODE (curated catalogues of phase-separating proteins) join to this topic on UniProt accession, but this paper contributes no rows to join to them.
integration.join_key: UniProt accession (would apply only to a handful of proteins: PD-1, LAT, GRB2, SOS1)
integration.bigger_question_one_sentence: Cannot be written usefully: with a handful of constructs there is nothing to integrate.

controls.positive_control: Would have been the paper's own finding that phosphorylating the PD-1 tyrosines abolishes inhibition; untestable without data.
controls.external_validation: None identified; no second source measures this specific quantity.

honest_claim_h3: No honest claim can be made, because there is no dataset: the paper's evidence lives in figure panels behind a subscription wall and was never deposited anywhere.

plain_idea.one_liner: Use a short protein sequence to predict whether it blocks or joins a signalling droplet inside T cells.
plain_idea.train_on: The project I considered would show the model the amino-acid sequence of a receptor tail or signalling-protein fragment, plus its phosphorylation state, for each tested construct. Number of examples: unknown, and almost certainly in the tens for this paper.
plain_idea.predict: Whether that fragment dissolves or supports a LAT (linker for activation of T cells) condensate, and by how much. The true answer would come from fluorescence microscopy of reconstituted droplets, scored by the authors in their figures.
plain_idea.why_worthwhile: Immunotherapy groups designing new inhibitory-receptor tails would get a quick screen for which motifs suppress T cell signalling, instead of reconstituting each one in vitro. Even a failed model would say whether sequence alone carries this information.

more_or_better_data.why: We would have zero rows: nothing was deposited. The named predictors (PICNIC, PSTP, LLPSense) were each trained on curated catalogues of hundreds to thousands of proteins, which is more than this paper could ever supply.

confidence_score.why: Replicate-level measurements are not available to us in any machine-readable form, so per-prediction uncertainty could not be estimated.

models_beatable.why: The relevant models are recent (2024-2026) and already use protein language model embeddings; with no training data of our own there is no route to beating them.

guaranteed_improvement.why: Fails the first condition outright: we have no dataset to add to an existing model, and no join key linking this paper's measurements to anything public.

ml_idea: Considered and abandoned: predict, from the amino-acid sequence of an inhibitory-receptor cytoplasmic tail, whether it suppresses LAT condensate formation, using frozen ESM-2 embeddings plus a small head. The idea is biologically interesting, but this paper supplies neither the labels nor the rows.

effort.compute_note: No estimates possible: no files were obtainable, so there is nothing to size.
effort.cheapest_killing_check: One HEAD request to the Science supplementary-materials URL. It returned HTTP 403, and Europe PMC reports hasSuppl=N and hasData=N. That took under a minute and killed the project.

verdict_reason: Part A1 fails, verified: nothing is deposited (no accession, no Zenodo, no Dryad, no Protein Data Bank entry, no preprint) and the Science supplement is behind a 403 subscription wall. Part A5 would fail too, since a mechanistic in vitro reconstitution paper tests tens of constructs, far below the ~400-row floor.
